overview: Four 1941 items: cross-references on Japan's refusal to let President Lines pass Shanghai's Nantao boom, barring foreigners from the Seto Inland Sea, and Vladivostok shipping statistics; plus a telegram on a columnist urging Japan close the Tsugaru and Soya straits against U.S.-linked shipping.

people.name: Frank P. Lockhart
people.role: U.S. Consul General at Shanghai; official associated with the referenced telegram

people.name: Joseph C. Grew
people.role: U.S. Ambassador to Japan and sender of the Tokyo telegram

people.name: Emoto
people.role: Columnist for the newspaper Hōchi; rendered by the OCR as “Emuto”

people.name: Sobokin
people.role: Official or sender named parenthetically in connection with the referenced Kobe telegram; precise identity and position are not stated

people.name: Angus I. Ward
people.role: U.S. diplomatic official at Vladivostok and apparent sender of the referenced telegram

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on President Lines vessels and the Nantao boom
subfiles.from: Frank P. Lockhart, Shanghai (sender of referenced telegram)
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to Shanghai telegram no. 678 concerning Japanese refusal to permit American President Lines vessels to pass the Nantao boom.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Japan refused to let American President Lines vessels pass Shanghai's Nantao boom, seen as disregarding American rights.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram on proposals to close the Tsugaru and Soya straits
subfiles.about: Grew reports a Hōchi column advocating closure of Japan’s northern straits to ships of hostile powers.
subfiles.summary: Columnist Emoto urges Japan close the Tsugaru and Soya straits in retaliation for the U.S. Panama Canal closure, warning of strategic shipments to Vladivostok and Hokkaido's defensive importance.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on restrictions on foreign travel in the Seto Inland Sea
subfiles.from: Sobokin, Kobe (as rendered in the text; sender of referenced telegram)
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to a Kobe telegram reporting a temporary prohibition on foreign travel in the Seto Inland Sea.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Japan barred all foreigners from the Seto Inland Sea in February, preventing American missionaries from traveling by steamer.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on merchant ships entering and clearing Vladivostok
subfiles.from: Angus I. Ward, Vladivostok (apparent sender of referenced telegram)
subfiles.about: The sheet refers to Vladivostok telegram no. 61 supplying requested details about merchant-ship arrivals and departures.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a telegram listing merchant vessels' names, flags, and dates entering and clearing Vladivostok.

interest: Shows 1941 Japanese navigation restrictions on American shipping, foreign travel, and Soviet port monitoring before Pearl Harbor.
